dep.acl.desc: A clause modifying a nominal, including relative clauses. 'the man WHO LEFT'
dep.acl.name: clausal modifier of noun
dep.advcl.desc: A clause modifying a predicate — time, condition, purpose, cause. 'IF IT RAINS, we stay.'
dep.advcl.name: adverbial clause modifier
dep.advmod.desc: An adverb or adverbial phrase modifying a predicate or modifier. 'She sang QUIETLY.'
dep.advmod.name: adverbial modifier
dep.amod.desc: An adjective modifying a nominal. 'the OLD dog'
dep.amod.name: adjectival modifier
dep.appos.desc: A nominal that renames or elaborates another nominal. 'Sam, MY BROTHER, called.'
dep.appos.name: appositional modifier
dep.aux.desc: A function word marking tense, aspect, mood, voice or polarity. 'She HAS left.'
dep.aux.name: auxiliary
dep.case.desc: An adposition or case affix attaching to a nominal. 'in THE garden' — 'in' attaches to 'garden'.
dep.case.name: case marking
dep.cc.desc: The coordinator itself, attached to the following conjunct. 'tea AND coffee'
dep.cc.name: coordinating conjunction
dep.ccomp.desc: A clausal object with its own subject. 'He says THAT YOU LIKE IT.'
dep.ccomp.name: clausal complement
dep.clf.desc: A numeral classifier accompanying a counted nominal. Common in East and Southeast Asian languages.
dep.clf.name: classifier
dep.compound.desc: A noun or verb compound. 'PHONE book'
dep.compound.name: compound
dep.conj.desc: A non-first element of a coordination, attached to the first conjunct. 'tea and COFFEE'
dep.conj.name: conjunct
dep.cop.desc: A linking verb joining a subject to a non-verbal predicate. 'She IS a teacher.'
dep.cop.name: copula
dep.csubj.desc: A clause functioning as the subject. 'WHAT SHE SAID matters.'
dep.csubj.name: clausal subject
dep.dep.desc: Fallback when the relation cannot be determined or no other label fits.
dep.dep.name: unspecified dependency
dep.det.desc: An article, demonstrative or quantifier specifying a nominal. 'THE dog'
dep.det.name: determiner
dep.discourse.desc: Interjections, fillers, and discourse particles. 'WELL, I think so.'
dep.discourse.name: discourse element
dep.dislocated.desc: A fronted or trailing element outside the normal argument structure. 'The book, I READ IT yesterday.'
dep.dislocated.name: dislocated element
dep.expl.desc: A semantically empty placeholder in subject position. 'THERE is a problem.'
dep.expl.name: expletive
dep.fixed.desc: A grammaticalised fixed expression treated as one unit. 'as WELL as'
dep.fixed.name: fixed multiword
dep.flat.desc: A headless multiword unit such as a personal name or date. 'Anna KARENINA'
dep.flat.name: flat multiword
dep.goeswith.desc: Joins parts of a word wrongly split in the original text.
dep.goeswith.name: goes with
dep.iobj.desc: A core argument other than subject or direct object, typically a recipient. 'She gave ME the book.'
dep.iobj.name: indirect object
dep.list.desc: Comparable items in a list, such as contact details in a signature block.
dep.list.name: list
dep.mark.desc: A word introducing a subordinate clause. 'I know THAT he left.'
dep.mark.name: marker
dep.nmod.desc: A nominal modifying another nominal, often possessive or prepositional. 'the roof OF THE HOUSE'
dep.nmod.name: nominal modifier
dep.nsubj.desc: A nominal that is the syntactic subject of a clause. 'The DOG barked.'
dep.nsubj.name: nominal subject
dep.nummod.desc: A numeral modifying a nominal. 'THREE books'
dep.nummod.name: numeric modifier
dep.obj.desc: The direct object — the second core argument of a transitive verb. 'She read the BOOK.'
dep.obj.name: object
dep.obl.desc: A non-core nominal, usually adverbial — place, time, manner. 'He slept IN THE GARDEN.'
dep.obl.name: oblique nominal
dep.orphan.desc: Links surviving dependents when their head has been elided in gapping.
dep.orphan.name: orphan
dep.parataxis.desc: Clauses joined without a coordinator or subordinator. 'He said it — I HEARD him.'
dep.parataxis.name: parataxis
dep.punct.desc: A punctuation mark, attached to the head of the phrase it delimits.
dep.punct.name: punctuation
dep.reparandum.desc: A disfluency that the speaker repairs. 'Go to the righ— TO THE LEFT.'
dep.reparandum.name: reparandum
dep.root.desc: The head of the whole sentence. Exactly one token per sentence; its head is left empty (shown as 0).
dep.root.name: root
dep.vocative.desc: A nominal used to address someone. 'MARY, come here.'
dep.vocative.name: vocative
dep.xcomp.desc: A predicative complement whose subject is supplied from outside. 'She tried TO LEAVE.'
dep.xcomp.name: open clausal complement

hdr.view.empty.title: No Corpus Loaded
help.faq.open.p1: Corpus: click Open in the header, or drag and drop a .jsonl corpus file onto the window.
help.faq.open.p2: Dictionary: after loading a corpus, a banner will appear if no dictionary is loaded. Click Load dictionary… in the banner, or use the Dictionary button in the header. LingCoT remembers which dictionary you last used with each corpus and shows it as a suggestion next time.
help.faq.open.p3: Replacing the dictionary: load a new dictionary at any time — your corpus is never affected. Useful for swapping between a general-purpose and a domain-specific dictionary.
help.faq.open.p4: Both file types use newline-delimited JSON (.jsonl) — one document per line for corpora, one entry per line for dictionaries.
help.faq.open.title: How to open & pair files?
help.faq.save.p1: LingCoT will offer to set up Autosave whenever you create or open a corpus. Click Yes, autosave and your changes will be written to disk automatically after each edit — no manual saves needed.
help.faq.save.p2: You can also configure save paths at any time by clicking Save in the header to open Project Files.
help.faq.save.p3: If your corpus is stored in a managed workspace folder, Export as .zip bundles the corpus, dictionary, and participants files into a single archive for sharing or backup. Your corpora live in ~/LingCoT-Data/corpora/ by default — outside the application folder, so they are never part of the app’s public code repository.
help.faq.save.title: How to save?
help.sidebar.title: Help
help.view.annotators.body:
People who annotate this corpus. Every edit records who made it.

Select yourself before annotating. Entries are kept in the corpus's participants file — treat it as personal data and share it only with collaborators covered by the same consent.
help.view.annotators.title: Annotators
help.view.corpus-new.body:
Name the corpus and set its language. Both can be changed later.

Title — used for the folder and file names.
Language — a code or name, e.g. tr, tur or Turkish. Translation needs this; if it is unrecognised LingCoT will suggest close matches.
help.view.corpus-new.title: New corpus
help.view.dict-browse.body:
Every entry, filtered and sorted.

On this screen

  • New entry — record a word that is not in the text yet. It asks for the type, part of speech, gloss and definition; everything else is set by editing the entry afterwards.
  • Filter — by type; Sort — by form, gloss or part of speech.
  • Export PDF — the current filtered list as a printable dictionary.
help.view.dict-browse.title: Dictionary
help.view.dict-edit.body:
Change the form, gloss, part of speech or type.

Editing a form does not rewrite corpus words already linked to this entry.
help.view.dict-edit.title: Editing the dictionary entry
help.view.dict.body:
One entry: its form, type, part of speech, gloss and examples.

Edit changes it. Pinned examples link it to sentences in the corpus.
help.view.dict.title: Dictionary entry
help.view.document-edit.body:
Corpus-level metadata.

Title — display name.
Language — code or name; used by translation.
Sources — where the text came from.
Notes — genre, register, collection method, ethics.

Save returns you to the document.
help.view.document-edit.title: Editing the document
help.view.document.body:
The whole corpus. Sections hold paragraphs, which hold sentences.

From here

  • Click a section to open it.
  • Edit — title, language, notes, sources.
  • + Section — add one.
help.view.document.title: Document
help.view.empty.body:
LingCoT builds and annotates interlinear text corpora. Everything stays on this machine.

Start here

  • Open — load a .jsonl corpus.
  • New — start an empty one.
  • Or drag a .jsonl file onto the window.

Where your work is kept

Corpora are saved in ~/LingCoT-Data/corpora/, outside the application folder. Back up that folder — copying the app folder will not save your work.
help.view.empty.title: Getting started
help.view.fallback.title: Help
help.view.lemma.body:
A lemma is a citation form that names a group — it is not a dictionary entry of its own, and it has no gloss or part of speech.

The two lists

  • Dictionary entries — entries whose Lemma field names this one. A lexicographer's statement about the lexeme.
  • Corpus tokens — words in the text annotated with this lemma. A per-occurrence annotation, and it is never reconciled with the list above automatically: the two are allowed to disagree.

A group with no entries is normal. For an agglutinative language the annotator usually does not want a dictionary entry for every surface form, so most lemmas are reached from the corpus side only.

When nothing at all points at a lemma record, this screen offers to delete it.
help.view.lemma.title: The lemma group
help.view.paragraph-add.body: Paste or type text. One sentence per line, or let LingCoT split on punctuation.
help.view.paragraph-add.title: New paragraph
help.view.paragraph-edit.body:
Edit the sentences as plain text, one per line. Saving re-splits the paragraph.

Sentences are matched by their text, so existing annotations survive an edit elsewhere in the paragraph.
help.view.paragraph-edit.title: Editing the paragraph
help.view.paragraph.body:
Sentences in order, each with its translation if it has one.

Translate all does every untranslated sentence here. Click a sentence to annotate it.
help.view.paragraph.title: Paragraph
help.view.search.body:
Search the corpus and read the results in context.

Pattern

  • * — any sequence, e.g. getir*.
  • (x) — optional, e.g. (un)happy.
  • Regex — raw expressions instead.

Scope

Level word or morpheme. Field text, gloss, transliteration or translation.

Views

  • Concordance — one line per hit, keyword centred.
  • Frequency — counts and distribution.
  • Collocates — what occurs near the hits.
help.view.search.title: Search
help.view.section-add.body:
Add a section to the document. You can paste text now or leave it empty and add paragraphs later.

Pasted text is split into paragraphs on blank lines.
help.view.section-add.title: New section
help.view.section-edit.body: Rename this section. Nothing inside it changes.
help.view.section-edit.title: Editing the section
help.view.section.body:
A chapter or episode. Click a paragraph to open it.

Edit renames the section. + Paragraph adds one.
help.view.section.title: Section
help.view.sentence-add.body: Add a sentence to this paragraph. Type the text; word splitting happens on save and can be corrected afterwards.
help.view.sentence-add.title: New sentence
help.view.sentence-edit.body:
Change the sentence text, its translation, or how it is split into words.

Words — one per line. Re-splitting keeps annotations on words whose form is unchanged.
Dependencies — set each word's head and relation. The root has no head.

Save moves you to the next sentence.
help.view.sentence-edit.title: Editing the sentence
help.view.sentence.body:
The interlinear block: each word with its gloss and morphemes.

On this screen

  • Click a word to annotate it.
  • Translate — fills the free translation.
  • Dependency parse — opens the arc diagram.
  • ← → — previous and next sentence. Arrow keys work too.
help.view.sentence.title: Sentence
help.view.sources.body:
Where the text came from: publications, recordings, speakers.

Documents reference sources by id, so one source can cover many documents.
help.view.sources.title: Sources
help.view.word-edit.body:
Fields

Transliteration — romanised or phonemic form.
Gloss — the whole word, e.g. person-PL-NOM.
Morphological parse — morphemes separated by hyphens, e.g. stem-suffix.
Morpheme rows — a gloss per morpheme. Appear as you type the parse.

Potential matches

  • Teal — a dictionary form found inside this word. Click to split it out.
  • Blue — a dictionary form matching a segment you already typed. Click to fill its gloss.
  • A chip dims once used.

Save moves you to the next word.
help.view.word-edit.title: Editing the word
help.view.word.body:
Everything recorded for one word: gloss, transliteration, morphemes, part of speech, dictionary link.

← → move to the previous or next word, skipping punctuation. Arrow keys work too.
help.view.word.title: Word
help.view.reader.title: Reader
help.view.reader.body:
The whole document, read continuously: text on the left, translation on the right. Nothing here can be edited.

Reading

  • Hover a sentence to see its translation highlighted.
  • Click a sentence, or press Enter on it, for its details: transliterations, every translation, comments.
  • Open in annotation view goes to the sentence's editor.

Getting here

Read on the document or a section. From a section, the reader opens at that section.
hint.amb.choosing: Choosing links this token and records the choice as yours
hint.dep.arc_caption: Arrows point from each token to its head. Click a token to open it.
hint.dep.editor: Set each token's head — the token it depends on. Choose "0 — root" for the one token that heads the sentence. Relation labels autocomplete from the Universal Dependencies set, but any label can be typed.
hint.dep.tokenize_first: This sentence has no tokens yet. Fill in Word Tokenization above and save, then reopen to assign dependencies.
offer.banner: The dictionary can fill {n} morpheme(s) across {forms} form(s)
offer.title: From the dictionary
offer.intro: Nothing here is written yet. Accepting a form writes {fields} field(s) and {links} link(s) in total, marked as the dictionary's work.
hint.derive.shown: Left empty, this reads from the morphemes:
hint.dict.dangling_lemmas: {n} lemma record(s) are missing, and entries or tokens still point at them. Rebuild:
hint.editor.annotators: All annotators who have edited this document or any of its contents.
hint.editor.bulk_text: Blank lines mark paragraph boundaries. Within each paragraph, each non-empty line is saved as exactly one sentence — your line breaks define the sentence structure. Existing annotations are preserved for sentences whose text is unchanged.
hint.editor.doc_sources: Participants or works this document is drawn from. Use + Add source to pick, or + New source to create one on the spot.
hint.editor.ingest: Each line is split into sentences by terminal punctuation (. ! ? 。！？ ؟ ۔ । ॥ …), so you can paste a full paragraph and get individual sentences. Words are tokenised on spaces; for non-space languages (Chinese, Japanese, …) word slots are left empty for manual annotation.
hint.editor.new_section: Leave blank to start with an empty section. Annotator for auto-parsed content is recorded as "automatically-parsed".
hint.editor.notes: Notes about genre, register, collection method, ethical considerations, etc.
hint.editor.parse_first: Enter a parse above (for example stem-suffix) to add morpheme rows.
hint.editor.save_to_dict: Saving opens a panel asking which of this word's forms should become dictionary entries, and what they should say. Nothing is written until you answer it, and an entry that already exists only has its empty fields filled.
hint.editor.sections: Rename sections and use the arrow buttons to reorder. Merge appends the next section's paragraphs into this one. The delete button removes the section (takes effect on Save). Paragraphs and annotations move with their section.
hint.editor.sources: Link sources (consultants, texts, media). Use + Add source to pick from existing ones, or + New source to create one on the spot.
hint.editor.word_forms: Space-separated word forms. Updates automatically from the text; edit manually to override.
hint.es.allomorphs: Conditioned variants, with the environment that conditions them. Stems have these too, not only affixes. Unconditioned variation goes in Variants.
hint.es.lemma_autocomplete: Type to autocomplete from existing lemmas, or enter a new form to create one.
hint.es.lemma_link: The abstract dictionary headword this form belongs to.
hint.es.lemma_link_morph: The abstract dictionary headword this form belongs to. Leave blank when adding a lemma entry itself.
hint.es.morph_segmentation: Separate morphemes with hyphens. Morpheme rows below update as you type.
hint.es.morphemes_csv: For word entries only: comma-separated morpheme forms that make up this word.
hint.es.semantic_domain: Thematic category for this entry, e.g. Body, Motion, Kinship. Used to organize the PDF dictionary.
hint.es.transliteration: Romanization, IPA, or any other script rendering — one per row with an optional label.
hint.es.usage_notes: Register, dialect, formality, or usage restrictions.
hint.es.variants: Spelling variants, dialectal forms, or historical forms. Each form links to its own dictionary entry if one exists.
hint.es.word_morpheme_list: For word entries: list the constituent morpheme forms. Each form links to its morpheme dictionary entry.
hint.lemma.ambiguous: {n} lemma records share this citation form — saving will not link it. Tell them apart in the lemma group view first.
hint.lemma.orphan: Nothing points at this lemma record.
hint.lemma.proposals: Suggested, from what is already here
hint.lemma.will_create: No match — saving will create this lemma
hint.lemma.will_link: Will link to the existing lemma
hint.sel.editor: What this entry combines with. Each frame is one alternative — a verb that is both transitive and intransitive has two.
hint.sent.edit_text: One sentence per line — each line is saved as exactly one sentence, regardless of punctuation. Merge two lines to join sentences; split a line into two to divide them. Existing annotations are preserved for sentences whose text is unchanged.
hint.sent.word_boundaries: Adjust word boundaries by editing spaces. Existing glosses and morpheme annotations are preserved for words whose form is unchanged.
hint.view.empty.body: Open a .jsonl or .json corpus file to get started, or create a new one.
hint.view.word.annotate_vs_lexicon: Annotate edits this token only; + Lexicon also creates a reusable dictionary entry that auto-applies to matching tokens.

sel.rel.adjunct.desc: An optional non-selected dependent, when you want it distinguished from modification.
sel.rel.argument.desc: An argument whose more specific relation is not being distinguished.
sel.rel.case_marking.desc: This entry marks the grammatical role of the selected item without contributing lexical content of its own. Case-marking adpositions, clitics and affixes. Contrast 'complement', where the adposition has its own meaning.
sel.rel.complement.desc: A non-subject argument selected by this entry, contributing its own lexical content. 'rumour that he left'. For an adposition or affix that only marks a role, use 'case marking'.
sel.rel.determination.desc: This entry fixes the reference of the selected item — definiteness, deixis or specificity. Determiner-noun: 'the dog', 'this dog'. Adds no property, so it is not modification.
sel.rel.direct_object.desc: The selected item is the direct object.
sel.rel.indirect_object.desc: The selected item is the indirect object, typically a recipient.
sel.rel.linking.desc: This entry joins the selected item into a larger structure — subordinator, complementizer or coordinator.
sel.rel.modification.desc: This entry adds a property to the selected item. Adjective-noun, adverb-verb, and adjuncts. Not determiners or numerals — see 'determination' and 'quantification'.
sel.rel.oblique.desc: A non-core argument of this entry, often case- or adposition-marked. This is the ARGUMENT's relation to its verb; for the marker's own relation to what it marks, use 'case marking'.
sel.rel.possessor.desc: The selected item is the possessor.
sel.rel.quantification.desc: This entry specifies the quantity or amount of the selected item. Numeral- or quantifier-noun: 'three dogs', 'many dogs'.
sel.rel.subject.desc: The selected item is the subject.
